title: An updated orbit of planet e and a new transit of d reduce the HD 191939 c mass tension between TESS transit times and radial velocities to about 2 sigma (coplanar N-body model, 2019-2024 data)
abstract: A prior campaign study found transit timing variations (TTVs) of HD 191939 c and d near their 4:3 period ratio and an N-body mass of c (2.4 +- 0.8 Earth masses) about 4 sigma below the radial-velocity (RV) mass. We timed all TESS 2-minute transits again (70 of b, 20 of c, 15 of d; 2019-2024; errors calibrated with 551 injected transits). This adds one transit of d (sector 49). We fitted 544 public RVs and made TTVFast N-body fits with a profile likelihood over the mass of c and an MCMC. The RV mass of c is robust: 7.5 +- 1.0 Earth masses, and 7.0-9.8 in every instrument and time subset. With the prior study's inputs, our global fit already gives 4.6, not 2.4, Earth masses. The prior study used an old period of the Saturn-mass planet e (101.12 d). The full RV set gives 101.71 +- 0.08 d. With this orbit, the TTV fit improves by delta chi2 = 14.6 at equal timing errors and the extra timing scatter of d decreases from 5.5 to 2.4 min. The TESS times then give m_c = 5.4 (+0.6/-0.7) Earth masses (MCMC 5.6 +- 0.5). The TTV and RV masses differ by 1.8-2.2 sigma, and together they give 6.1 (+0.5/-0.6) Earth masses. Without the sector-49 transit, the TTV mass is 4.6 and the tension is 2.3-2.6 sigma. The fits need nearly aligned eccentricities of about 0.09 (c) and 0.08 (d), and these orbits are stable for 10,000 years. TESS will observe the star again in 2027-2028; we give posterior forecasts (68% widths about 2 min for c and 4 min for d). Limitations: a coplanar model, one timing pipeline, a fixed timing jitter, and an approximate (prior-based) combination of the TTV and RV data instead of a simultaneous dynamical RV fit.
